blogs.title: Bitten, Septic, and Subtle: Recognizing Capnocytophaga canimorsus Early
blogs.description: Dog and cat exposures can progress from benign wounds to fulminant sepsis with DIC. This post reviews clinical red flags for Capnocytophaga canimorsus (rapid sepsis, leukopenia, DIC, acral ischemia), empiric antibiotic choices that cover Capnocytophaga (e.g., piperacillin–tazobactam, carbapenems; caution with beta-lactamase–stable options), the organism’s slow culture growth and role of molecular diagnostics, and practical pathways for early identification and de-escalation once cultures result—even in immunocompetent hosts.

blogs.title: When DIC Masks a TMA: Unpacking the Sepsis-to-CM-HUS Transition
blogs.description: Early sepsis/DIC can obscure an evolving thrombotic microangiopathy. We dissect distinguishing features and timelines: falling hemoglobin with undetectable haptoglobin, rising LDH, schistocytosis, persistent thrombocytopenia despite resolution of coagulopathy, and kidney injury out of proportion to the septic course. We contrast pathophysiology of sepsis-associated DIC vs complement-mediated HUS, discuss why C3/C4 can be normal, and highlight the tipping points that should pivot clinicians from DIC-centric care to TMA workup and therapy.

blogs.title: MAHA + Thrombocytopenia + AKI at the Bedside: A Rapid TMA Algorithm
blogs.description: A pragmatic, time-sensitive approach for adults with suspected TMA: immediate labs (smear for schistocytes, LDH, haptoglobin, bilirubin), calculate PLASMIC, send ADAMTS13, test for STEC (stool PCR), and screen for secondary causes. We outline when to start plasma exchange as a bridge, how to triage away from TTP when ADAMTS13 >10%, and when to pivot quickly to complement blockade. Practical tips include handling false-positive DATs, transfusion strategies, and coordinating hematology/nephrology input without delaying definitive therapy.

blogs.title: Pulling the Trigger on Eculizumab: Infection Timing, Vaccines, and Prophylaxis
blogs.description: Complement blockade saves kidneys in CM-HUS but invites infectious risk. This post covers real-world timing of eculizumab in the setting of recent bacteremia (why many wait for culture clearance), vaccine strategy (MenACWY and MenB; ideal 2-week lead time vs same-day with antibiotic prophylaxis), antimicrobial choices (e.g., penicillin/ampicillin alternatives if allergic), and monitoring. We discuss balancing ongoing sepsis care with the morbidity of delayed complement inhibition, and how to communicate risks to patients.

blogs.title: Complement Testing in the Real World: Normal C3/C4, Post-PEX Labs, and Genetics
blogs.description: Interpreting complement studies during an evolving TMA is tricky. We explain why C3/C4 can be normal in CM-HUS, how AH50/alternative pathway assays are altered by plasma exchange and eculizumab, and the limited but meaningful yield of extended genetic testing (factors H/I/B, MCP/CD46, anti–factor H antibodies). Learn which tests to draw before PEX/eculizumab, how to make sense of results obtained after treatment has started, and how findings should influence duration of complement blockade and relapse surveillance.

blogs.title: Kidney Biopsy in TMA: When It Helps, When It Hurts
blogs.description: Do you biopsy the anuric, thrombocytopenic patient with suspected TMA? We discuss indications, timing once platelets are safe, and how histology refines diagnosis and prognosis (fibrin thrombi, ischemic glomeruli, ATN, crescents; absence of immune complex deposition). We also cover procedural risk mitigation in coagulopathic patients, and how biopsy findings inform the decision to commit to prolonged complement inhibition versus expectant management if secondary TMA is suspected.
